original_requirement: EG13/S05: competing foreground/background updates validate their base and cannot overwrite a newer head; physical deletion versus unfinished workers/cached incarnations was an explicit remaining gap.

demonstrated_failure.outcome: Actual public foreground update paused before publication: delete_project returned success while removing the project record, published head and update mutex before the update settled. Owned fixture cleanup was empty.

implemented: Deletion preserves the existing update lane and serializes runtime opening, cache eviction and physical cleanup.
Cooperatively cancel and join captured jobs before taking their update lane; the entire deletion task and blocking cleanup survive RPC cancellation.

Serialize index/update job registration with runtime admission; recheck genuinely tracked running jobs before cleanup. Late admissions refuse with retry; stale persisted running rows after restart do not block deletion forever.

Refuse cleanup before registry/graph mutation while cached, evicted, cloned, detached-operation or source-only catalog owners remain; hold local catalog admission and existing process file lock during deletion.

Dreamer, immune and integrity cold opens share runtime admission; queued initial-index jobs recheck cancellation/registration before creating stores. GC retains its already-serialized uncached loader.
Disable watches after storage admission. Propagate physical removal errors with delete-by-ID retry; never report failed cleanup as successful deletion.

cases: Foreground publication must settle before deletion; stable mutex retained; stores absent after success; identical ID re-registration indexes complete replacement source.
Source-only reader after engine/cache release refuses deletion without changing published data; release allows retry.
Queued index job is cancelled and joined without recreating stores or job records.
Cancelling delete RPC during job drain still finishes the owned deletion.
Late background job admission refuses destructive cleanup, settles, and permits retry; new job registration after deletion fails without creating metadata.
Actual AppState close/reopen permits cleanup of an ownerless persisted running job.
Windows exclusive file-handle obstruction causes explicit physical-cleanup error; retry after release removes remaining directory.
validation.native_scope: Foreground/source-reader/late-update cases use actual local native vector storage, with complete source body/PK/vector membership checks. Queued jobs are cancelled before opening stores. Stale-job and filesystem-obstruction fixtures intentionally use fts_only in either compiled build.
validation.registration_regression: Existing foreground_and_background_registration_publish_their_own_complete_initial_generation passes in native and no-vector builds.

limits: Release build, isolated public MCP verification and installed verification remain pending.
Original S05 remains partial: this is a bounded deletion/publication lifecycle delivery, not proof of every store-commit, crash, physical catalog replacement or cross-platform cross-process boundary.
Physical cleanup failure can follow registry/graph removal; the returned error identifies partial cleanup and supports retry by ID.
No external CodeRabbit review was performed; trusted CLI was unauthenticated. Independent local source and helper reviews are retained.

temporary_resources.fixtures: All completed test fixture inventories are empty. Runtime shutdown precedes fixture cleanup, including failure/unwinding.
temporary_resources.retained: Test logs, review receipts, empty runner TEMP containers and prepared release helpers. No preexisting directory cleanup.
